svg.title: P007 · Discount amount and percentage per product
svg.desc: One row per product, including products with an unknown discount. Mug saves 100 − 80 = 20 and Lamp saves 200 − 150 = 50. Sticker keeps its row with a NULL discount. Mug saves 20 / 100 = 20%. Lamp saves 50 / 200 = 25%. The zero-price guard leaves Sticker's percentage NULL. Lamp's 25% leads Mug's 20%. SQLite places Sticker's NULL last in descending order.
svg.text: Discount amount and percentage per product
One row per product, including products with an unknown discount.
Sticker has a market price of zero. Does the row survive? What goes in its discount
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
How much money does each buyer save?
Mug saves 100 − 80 = 20 and Lamp saves 200 − 150 = 50. Sticker keeps its row with a NULL discount.
Which price belongs in the denominator?
Mug saves 20 / 100 = 20%. Lamp saves 50 / 200 = 25%. The zero-price guard leaves Sticker's percentage NULL.
How do we rank an unknown percentage?
Lamp's 25% leads Mug's 20%. SQLite places Sticker's NULL last in descending order.
